small_guidance:
- Fuse the softmax into the GEMM epilogue when N fits a single program tile: switch to a "split-K-free, persistent along N" design where each program owns an entire row (BLOCK_N == N == 8192) so the GELU output stays in registers/SRAM and softmax is done before the store — eliminating the full read/write of the M×N=1024×8192 GELU tensor that currently dominates.
- If full-row fusion is too large for SRAM, do a two-pass row-resident softmax kernel that reads the GELU output once with vectorized loads (BLOCK_N=8192, num_warps=16, num_stages=2) and combine max+sum in a single online pass to halve the softmax memory traffic.
- Add narrower GEMM autotune configs targeting M=1024, N=K=8192 (e.g. BLOCK_M=64/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=64, num_warps=8, num_stages=4; BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=128) and consider pre-transposing W once in __init__ so the inner B load is contiguous along N instead of using swapped strides.
large_guidance:
- Redesign as a row-parallel fused matmul→GELU→softmax kernel: one program per row (or small row-block) with N held in registers/SMEM. Compute the full row's GEMM into a register tile, apply GELU in-place, do an online softmax (running max + running sum) with a single rescaling pass, then store the normalized row — removing the intermediate GELU tensor entirely and turning the softmax launch into zero extra global traffic.
- If the row doesn't fit (N=8192, M-tile rows × 8192 floats too large), use a two-stage persistent design: stage 1 computes GEMM+GELU and writes to a workspace while simultaneously reducing per-row max and sum (fused row-reduction over the K-completed tile, using atomics or a per-row scratch); stage 2 is a lightweight normalize kernel that reads workspace once and writes output. This trades one pass for the current three.
- Pre-transpose and pad the weight to (K, N) contiguous-N at init time, store as a buffer, so the GEMM uses stride_bn=1 — this typically gives 10-20% on Ada for K=N=8192 GEMMs and removes the strided B-load pattern.
